missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Портрет' stays in the nominative as the subject of 'висит'. 'Старый' is the agreeing masculine adjective, and 'на стене' gives the location.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Портрет' is the accusative direct object of 'нарисовал'; for this inanimate masculine noun the accusative matches the nominative. 'Её' shows whose portrait it is.
Strategic focus: Genitive of absence. 'Портрета' takes the genitive after 'нет' to express what is missing. 'Этого' agrees in the masculine genitive, and 'в музее' sets the place.
Strategic focus: Accusative after на. 'Портрет' is accusative after 'на' with the verb 'смотрел', expressing the direction of the gaze. 'Долго' adds duration to the looking.
Strategic focus: Instrumental after под. 'Портретом' takes the instrumental case after 'под' to show position below. 'Маленький стул' is the nominative subject of 'стоит'.
Strategic focus: Prepositional after на. 'Портрете' is in the prepositional case after 'на' to mark where something is depicted. 'Молодой король' is the nominative subject.
Strategic focus: Accusative gift with dative recipient. 'Портрет' is the accusative object of 'подарил', and 'бабушке' is the dative recipient. 'Свой' marks it as his own portrait.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Портреты' is the nominative plural subject of 'висят'. 'Семейные' agrees in the plural, and 'в галерее' is prepositional, giving the location.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural after много. 'Портретов' takes the genitive plural after 'много'. 'Старинных' agrees in the genitive plural, describing the antique portraits.

missions.phrase: Этот портрет очень похож на оригинал.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject with comparison. 'Портрет' is the nominative subject. 'Этот' agrees in the masculine, and 'похож на оригинал' uses the accusative to state the resemblance.
